s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral skin hardening with limited joint motion
salient_findings: Unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock
Limited motion of the right limb joint
key_facts: 11-year-old boy
7-year history of progressive skin hardening
Stony-hard plaque on the right thigh and buttock
Loss of skin elasticity
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation
Normal routine blood tests
Normal autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
MRI showed slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Histopathological findings: normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts
Increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis

differentials: Panniculitis Associated with Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency
per_call: Panniculitis Associated with Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency

shortlist.label: Linear Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of progressive unilateral skin hardening and limited joint motion

shortlist.label: Morphea
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by stony-hard plaques and loss of skin elasticity, consistent with the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Lipedematous Sclerosing Panniculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Involves the subcutaneous tissue and can cause skin hardening, matching the patient's MRI and histopathological findings

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic Fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause skin thickening and limited joint motion, although the absence of eosinophilia in laboratory tests makes it less likely

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Although the patient's symptoms are more localized, scleroderma is a possible diagnosis given the presence of skin hardening and limited joint motion

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of progressive unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock, along with loss of skin elasticity, mild hypertrichosis, and hyperpigmentation, is consistent with Linear Scleroderma. The histopathological findings of normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts, as well as the increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Morphea
rejected.why: Morphea typically presents with well-defined, circular, or oval patches of sclerosis, which is not consistent with the patient's stony-hard plaque involving the right thigh and buttock.

rejected.label: Lipedematous Sclerosing Panniculitis
rejected.why: Lipedematous Sclerosing Panniculitis is characterized by a painful, indurated plaque on the lower legs, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation of a stony-hard plaque on the right thigh and buttock.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic Fasciitis
rejected.why: Eosinophilic Fasciitis is characterized by rapid onset of swelling and induration of the skin, often with eosinophilia, which is not consistent with the patient's 7-year history of progressive skin hardening and normal laboratory tests.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: Scleroderma is a systemic disease that typically presents with widespread skin thickening, Raynaud's phenomenon, and internal organ involvement, which is not consistent with the patient's localized skin hardening and normal laboratory tests.
